wil9jx:395: The difficulty in detecting LLMReaper lies in the fact that it satisfies multiple low-detectability conditions at once: the attack tool is part of the legitimate browser extension ecosystem; the attack behavior occurs within the victim's local browser process (rather than through network traffic whose anomalies could be detected); and the stolen data is content actively typed in by the user rather than system-level credential modification. Among existing security products, endpoint detection and response (EDR) solutions typically monitor process-level behavior and network connections, but extensions run inside a restricted browser sandbox; network security devices (firewalls, IDS/IPS) cannot see the message passing inside an extension, nor can they distinguish a user's legitimate HTTPS traffic to AI websites from an extension's data exfiltration. Mitigations such as "checking and removing unused extensions" work at the individual user level, but are nearly useless in enterprise environments with a bring-your-own-extension policy — security teams cannot control extension choices on employees' personal devices. Multi-browser profile isolation provides session-level isolation, but cannot prevent lateral data movement between extensions within the same profile.
